technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The aim and product of capitalist production: value taken above the value of labour-power.
Unpaid labour performed beyond the necessary labour; the thing capital absorbs.
The worker's capacity to work, which capital buys at its daily value.
Labour time needed to reproduce the worker's own labour-power.
Means of production whose value passes into the product but creates no new value.
Money spent on labour-power; the only part that produces surplus-value.
Ratio of surplus labour to necessary labour, also called the degree of exploitation.
Total surplus-value of all labourers employed: variable capital times the rate.
Money value of what the worker needs to be reproduced; held constant in this chapter.
Length of daily labour, the object of struggle between capital and workers.
Time measured as labour; under capital all the worker's disposable time becomes labour-time.
Maintaining the working class by replacing the worker's used-up capacity.
Capital's drive to grow in value; the purpose that governs the working day.
Shifts of different children or young persons covering the day, used to evade the Factory Acts.
Workers in excess of capital's immediate need for surplus labour.
The capitalist as capital in human form, controlling labour.
Value expressed in money, used to say how much money is needed to become a capitalist.
Labour viewed as making use values, contrasted with the process of creating surplus-value.
All labour of a society added up as one collective working day.
New value created by living labour, excluding the transferred value of constant capital.
The least capital needed to employ one worker year-round, so one can become a capitalist.
Machines and materials (dead) versus the worker's activity (living), inverted under capital.

Vulgar economy, in opposition to Spinoza, takes ignorance as justification.

numbers_formulas_tables.what: Formula S = (s/v) x V, with P x (a'/a) x n, printed as a broken three-line fraction; restore cleanly
Symbols: S mass, s surplus-value per labourer, v variable capital per labourer, V total variable capital, P labour-power value, a'/a exploitation, n workers
Worked example: 300s advanced, 100 labourers, 50% rate gives 150s; or 150s at 12-hour day
Limit example: 1,500s, 500 labourers, 100%, 12-hour day gives 1,500s; 300s, 100 labourers, 200%, 18-hour day gives 600s; cap of 1,200s
Social working day: a million labourers x 10 hours = ten million hours
Capital minimum rising eight times with more labourers; footnote on homologous chemical series C_nH_2n+2
Weekly hours: 78 1/2 hours average, 84 hours in six weeks; 152 children and 140 adults
Railway fireman's weekly hours: 29 hours 15 minutes straight; 88 hours 30 minutes in a week; paid 6 1/4 days
Child shift records: 12-hour turns, 3 nights a week, 36 hours consecutive
Relay timings: 5.30 a.m. to 1.30 p.m. one set, 1.30 to 8.30 p.m. another
Wage cuts: 10% general, 8 1/3% on shortening to 11 hours, double again at 10 hours; at least 25% overall
Table of pulmonary death-rates per 100,000 by district and occupation, Greenhow 1861
Working day for young persons and women: 10 to 10 1/2 hours Mon-Fri, 7 1/2 Saturday; 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.

voice_attribution_risks.note: Mr. Smith's 'we' and 'Machine-work is not great' are his words; Marx's mockery sits in the surrounding sentences.
Otley's quote contains Marx's parenthetical '(What generosity!)' inserted in the quoted text.
Sanderson's quote contains Marx's interjection '(what queer-headed folk!)' inside it.
Commission quote interrupted by Marx's '(What cynical naivete!)' and '(What mealy-mouthed phraseology!)'.
Ure's denunciation is stated as a rhetorical question before Marx's own view; risk of reading it as Marx's claim.
Macaulay's 'progress' statement is quoted, then answered with 'What eyes, and especially what ears!'.
The Essay author's quote contains Marx's gloss '(he means capital as we shall soon see)'.
'The pretended Ten Hours' Act was thus simple humbug' is ambiguous: whose view is this, the masters' or Marx's own.
Irony about the Emancipation Act; Marx's sarcasm should not be read as endorsing Parliament.
The 'millennium' and 'perjured Free-traders' are Marx's irony in a historical summary.
Inspector Howell's 'judicial farces' is a quote; Marx endorses the complaint but not the stipendiary-magistrate remedy.
Ure is called 'philosopher of the Factory' with sarcasm; the claim about the 'slavery of the Factory Acts' is Ure's, reported by Marx.
Carlile letter is presented with Marx's sarcasm ('very intelligent gentleman', 'grotesquely naive').
'Vulgar economy which has really learnt nothing' is quoted without a source; reader may think it is Marx's own claim.

irony_examples.note: Otley: 'What generosity!' and 'I can understand the loss of time not being liked', mocking a boss's sympathy.
Smith's 'royal we' is set against his workers, mocking the pluralis majestatis.
Free-trade 'sophistry' that makes white black; Protagoras and the Eleatics invoked to mock it.
'roused not the heart of the public but its stomach'; 'elective grace' mocks Christian capitalists.
Coroner's jury verdict described as a lesson in good manners for the doctor.
Tory and Carlyle's sympathy for slaves dismissed as 'the bubble of Tory sympathy' that has burst.
'Sandersonian reason'; the Sandersons' profit-driven claim dressed as principled.
Mr. Glass-Capital, drunk and shouting 'Britons never shall be slaves'.
Macaulay's 'progress' answered with 'What eyes, and especially what ears!'.
The 'faithful Eckart of capital' and the 'House of Terror' called an ideal.
Parliament's 'delicate consideration' for manufacturers; freedom 'drop by drop'.
Free-trade 'millennium' and the Free-trade 'perjured' mock the repeal era.
'Lynx eye of Capital' used for the loophole-seeking manufacturers.
Shylock-clinging: capital insisting on the bond's letter.
'unctuous Free-traders, perspiring with the love of humanity'.
'Pharisees of Political Economy' claiming credit for a discovery forced on them.
Carlile's 'very intelligent gentleman' and 'grotesquely naive' passage.

hard_passages.why: Long dense rhetorical paragraph on capital's were-wolf hunger; many compressed clauses and metaphors.
Long sentence contrasting capital in embryo with capital in maturity; many 'thus' links.
Relay-system logic with many sub-clauses; hard to follow who does what.
Stage-metaphor sentence about shifting operatives; extended analogy with Fourier.
Dense legal regulation of hours and meal times; rewriter must preserve exact rule.
Final lines on free agent and vampire; dense logic about contract and freedom.
Symbols S, s, v, V, P, a'/a, n defined in one paragraph; needs precise restatement.
Formula printed as broken fragments; the structure is hard to recover from the text.
Compensation argument between variable capital and rate of surplus-value; many numbers.
Limits argument with multiple numerical cases and dense phrasing.
Long argument about constant vs. variable capital and the value law; dense terms.
Analogy to 0/0 and appearance vs. law; ambiguous references to classical economy.
Minimum-capital argument with Hegelian quantity-into-quality; long, many clauses.
Inversion of dead and living labour; sophisticated analogy about capital and labour.
